one_liner: Peer-reviewed AVX-512F reduced-radix large-integer multiplication for Xeon Phi Knights Landing, reported about 2.5x faster than GMP; no code.
what_it_does: A research paper (Edamatsu and Takahashi, 'Acceleration of Large Integer Multiplication with Intel AVX-512 Instructions', IEEE HPCC 2018) that vectorizes multi-precision integer multiplication with AVX-512F on the Knights Landing Xeon Phi and compares execution time and instruction counts with GMP. No source, library or API attributable to the paper has been published, so it is a technique to reimplement, not a replacement you can link for mpz_mul/mpn_mul.
how_it_is_fast: AVX-512F has no 64x64-bit vector multiply; VPMULUDQ (_mm512_mul_epu32) gives eight 32x32-to-64-bit products per instruction. With a reduced-radix representation (limbs narrower than 32 bits) each 64-bit accumulator keeps headroom, so the column sums of the product can be built from many vector multiply-adds before carries are propagated in a final normalization pass. On Knights Landing, whose scalar cores are weak, this vector path beats GMP's scalar mpn code; the exact limb width and multiplication algorithm used in the paper are not documented in anything readable this session.
when_to_use: Designing a multi-precision multiply for cores that have AVX-512F but not AVX-512IFMA, such as Knights Landing, where GMP's scalar path is slow.
Throughput-oriented number crunching on many-core Xeon Phi nodes that still run, as a reference for vectorizing the column sums of a multi-limb product.
As the baseline when evaluating the same authors' later AVX-512IFMA paper, which reports up to about 3.07x over this AVX-512F approach.
when_not_to_use: You need code you can run: nothing is published and attributed, so has_code is false.
CPUs with AVX-512IFMA: the authors' own IFMA version (sibling entry) reports up to about 3.07x over their AVX-512F one.
Mainstream x86 cores with fast scalar 64-bit multiply and carry chains: the 2.5x is specific to Knights Landing, and the gain elsewhere is not documented.
Very large operands where GMP uses Toom-Cook or FFT multiplication: the operand-size range of the result is not documented.
New deployments: Knights Landing (Xeon Phi) is discontinued.

integration.min_toolchain: not documented (needs AVX-512F intrinsics or assembler support)
integration.platforms: x86-64 with AVX-512F; measured on Intel Knights Landing (exact Xeon Phi model not documented)

gotchas: Evidence is snippet only: ieeexplore document 8622797 and semanticscholar are egress-blocked, so GMP version, operand sizes, compiler, flags and the exact CPU are unknown.
Reduced-radix limbs need split and recombine passes to and from 32- or 64-bit limbs; whether the reported time includes that conversion is not documented.

Hibari-K/bigint_mul_avx512f matches the topic and period (28-bit split/combine, _mm512_mul_epu32, 'naive algorithm', Makefile for Intel icc -xMIC-AVX512 on Knights Landing) but names no authors or paper, has no timing harness, no GMP comparison and no license; do not treat it as this paper's artifact.
Knights Landing results lean on its weak scalar cores, so a 2.5x win over GMP there says little about Skylake-SP or later server parts.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Read it only as a design reference for AVX-512F-only hardware; on IFMA-capable CPUs prefer the same authors' AVX-512IFMA design, and for runnable code CGBN (GPU, 43.5x average on low multiplication vs 20-core GMP), lea-gl's batched AVX-512 Montgomery code or FLINT (large sizes) are the practical picks.
verified_claims_summary: Two search-engine summaries of the abstract (paper not opened) say the AVX-512F implementation is about 2.5x faster in execution time than GMP for large-integer multiplication on Knights Landing, also comparing instruction counts. GMP version, operand sizes, compiler, flags and the exact Xeon Phi model are not documented.
status_note: A 2018 peer-reviewed paper with no released code on discontinued hardware, so it is reference material only; it could be re-tiered to B once a verifier can read the paper.
